newsitem.title: USA: Business inventories up slightly in November.
newsitem.headline: Business inventories up slightly in November.

text.p: Inventories held by businesses barely rose in November as brisk sales kept goods from piling up at manufacturing, wholesale and retail levels, the Commerce Department said on Wednesday.
Total business inventories were up 0.1 percent in November to a seasonally adjusted $1.01 trillion, after an 0.5 percent rise in October, the department said.
Wall Street economists had forecast November inventories would rise by 0.3 percent.
The biggest change occurred among retailers' inventories, which shrank 0.4 percent to $314.05 billion after a 0.8 percent October increase.

Department officials said it was the first drop in retail inventories in eight months, since they fell 0.9 percent in March. Most of the decline in retail inventories in November occurred at automobile dealers and at furniture stores.

By contrast, manufacturers' inventories rose 0.4 percent in November to $439.89 billion after a 0.3 percent October rise, while wholesale inventories edged up 0.1 percent to $285.02 billion following a 0.3 percent October increase.
Business sales were up in November by 0.6 percent to $729.83 billion, a third consecutive monthly increase after a 0.4 percent rise in October.
The small rise in November inventories, coupled with relatively strong sales, may signal that a long-running inventory correction was largely completed by the beginning of November, economists said.
They said that once stocks of goods were brought into line with sales, inventory investment could begin to add to the pace of economic activity.
The inventory-to-sales ratio -- a measure of how long it would take to sell existing stocks at the current pace -- remained at 1.39 months' worth in November, the same as in September and October.
